scenario: Aug 3: President Trump canceled planned US strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure over the weekend at the request of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the UAE, Qatar and Iran, and said a deal covering the 'complete and total opening' of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's denuclearization is imminent, with fresh talks set to begin today (Newsweek, ABC News, Aug 2). Iran's FM Araghchi said Oman-mediated negotiations on reopening Hormuz have reached their final stages, though Iran still insists on retaining control and collecting transit fees (Xinhua, Aug 2-3). Markets priced out risk premium sharply: Brent fell 4.9% to $83.61/bbl (Investing.com, Aug 3); TTF fell 5.1% to 56.06 EUR/MWh (Trading Economics, Aug 3); JKM's CFD reference held near $21.45/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Jul 31). The strait remains physically closed, with the last reviewed transit count still 6 vessels/day (Windward, Jul 27). Tail falls to 45%.

categories.label: Food & Agriculture
categories.supplyChainImpact: Middle East fertilizer and energy exports remain constrained by wartime-low Hormuz traffic. Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 39 ships in Jul 20-26, down from 82 the prior week. This sustains freight and input-cost risk for Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia planting chains, while Qatar force majeure remains extended to mid-September.
